Thus he showed me: behold, the Lord stood beside a wall made by a plumb line, with a plumb line in his hand.
Yahweh said to me, “Amos, what do you see?” I said, “A plumb line.” Then the Lord said, “Behold, I will set a plumb line in the midst of my people Israel. I will not again pass by them any more.
The high places of Isaac will be desolate, and the sanctuaries of Israel will be laid waste; and I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.”
b: God first let Amos see the plague of locusts and the judgment of fire. Each time Amos saw the people about to be judged, he did not gloat; he immediately interceded: “How could Jacob stand? For he is small.” God heard the prophet’s prayer and twice withheld the coming disaster. We see that God does not punish lightly; he is full of mercy and glad to hear intercession.

The third vision, however, was different. God held a plumb line in his hand, showing that he would measure his people’s lives by justice and truth. If a wall is built crooked, a plumb line reveals it; if a life drifts from God, it needs to be corrected by God’s truth. God’s love is real, but so is his justice.

Israel had long lived in rebellion. Religious activity continued, but their hearts were far from God. So God no longer gave only warnings; he pointed to the root of the problem: their lives had departed from his standard. The problem was not with God’s plumb line; it was that their lives had become crooked.

Today God’s word is the plumb line for our lives. Many people measure right and wrong by their feelings and set their direction by the world’s standards, but true wisdom lets God’s truth correct our lives. When we are willing to accept God’s light and correction, we can walk the upright and blessed path.
a: Intercede for others
Learn, like Amos, to pray to God for the weak.
Accept God’s searching light
Let God show you what in your life needs adjusting.
Take God’s word as your standard
Don’t follow the world’s values; obey God’s truth.
q: Am I living by my own standard, or adjusting myself according to God’s plumb line?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for being not only full of mercy but also full of justice. Help me come before You often to receive Your light and correction. If any part of my life has drifted from You, guide me to turn back to You. Give me also a compassionate heart, willing to pray and keep watch for the people around me. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will take God’s word as my plumb line and walk in the way that pleases him.

t: He Can Turn Mourning into Dancing
v: Sing to Yahweh, you saints of his! Give thanks to his holy name.
For his anger is but for a moment. His favor is for a lifetime. Weeping may stay for the night, but joy comes in the morning.
As for me, I said in my prosperity, “I will never be moved.”
You, Yahweh, when you favored me, made my mountain stand strong; but when you hid your face, I was troubled.
I cried to you, Yahweh. I made supplication to the Lord:
“What profit is there in my destruction, if I go down to the pit? Will the dust praise you? Will it declare your truth?
Hear, Yahweh, and have mercy on me. Yahweh, be my helper.”
You have turned my mourning into dancing for me. You have removed my sackcloth, and clothed me with gladness,
to the end that my heart may sing praise to you, and not be silent. Yahweh my God, I will give thanks to you forever!
b: Looking back on his life, David discovered that the greatest danger is often not hardship but forgetting to depend on God in times of ease. He once said, “I will never be moved.” But when God hid his face for a moment, he was immediately terrified. He learned that all stability comes not from his own ability but from God’s grace.

When David fell into pain and the depths, he did not run from God; he cried out to him even more earnestly. He brought his fear, helplessness, and tears before God. True faith is not never weeping; it is still praying while we weep, still believing that God hears our cry.

Then David experienced God’s wonderful work. God did not let tears be the end of the story. He turned his mourning into dancing and exchanged his sackcloth for joy. This is how God always works: he can bring dawn into the night, hope into despair, and blessing out of pain.

“Weeping may stay for the night, but joy comes in the morning” has comforted people through the ages. Perhaps the night has not yet passed, perhaps the problem is not fully solved, but God promises that his favor is for a lifetime. If we hold fast to God, we will surely see his deliverance and guidance.
a: Depend on God even in good times
Don’t mistake God’s grace for your own ability.
Cry out to God in the valley
Bring your sorrows and burdens to the Lord.
Believe God can turn circumstances around
The night won’t last forever; God will bring a new morning.
q: Am I going through a dark night right now? Am I willing to believe God is still at work?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for being a God full of grace and mercy. In good times, keep me thankful and humble; in hard times, help me not lose faith. Thank You that You can turn mourning into dancing and sorrow into joy. Whatever my situation, may I hold fast to You, believing Your grace is always enough for me. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will trust God’s grace, believing he will bring my night into morning.

t: Saved by Grace
v: You were dead through your trespasses and sins,
in which you once walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, of the spirit who now works in the children of disobedience;
among whom we also all once lived in the lust of our flesh, doing the desires of the flesh and of the mind, and were by nature children of wrath, even as the rest.
But God, being rich in mercy, for his great love with which he loved us,
even when we were dead through our trespasses, made us alive together with Christ—by grace you have been saved—
and raised us up with him, and made us to sit with him in the heavenly places in Christ Jesus,
that in the ages to come he might show the exceeding riches of his grace in kindness toward us in Christ Jesus.
For by grace you have been saved through faith, and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God,
not of works, that no one would boast.
For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared before that we would walk in them.
b: Paul first reminds us that humanity’s greatest problem is not bad circumstances but a life cut off from God. Those apart from God may be alive in body, but they are dead in spirit, able only to follow the currents of the world and their own desires. By our own effort we cannot truly solve the problem of sin and death.

But the most precious turn in this passage is “But God.” When people were powerless to save themselves, God, in his rich mercy and great love, reached out to save us. He did not wait for us to become good before loving us; while we were still dead in sin, he made us alive through Jesus Christ.

So salvation is wholly God’s grace. We cannot buy it with good deeds or earn eternal life by merit. Salvation is a gift freely given by God, and we receive it by faith. This gives all the glory to God, not to ourselves.

But grace is not the finish line; it is a new starting point. God saves us not merely so we can go to heaven someday but so we can live a new life. The passage says we are God’s workmanship, his masterpiece made by his own hand. When we let Christ rule within us, we can live the good life God prepared, and become a blessing to others.
a: Give thanks for God’s salvation
Remember that you are saved entirely by God’s grace.
Don’t rely on your own merit
Give all the glory to God.
Live out a new life
Each day do good and serve according to God’s heart.
q: Am I still trying to please God by my own effort, or am I truly living in God’s grace?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for saving me with Your great love while I was still weak and living in sin. Thank You for giving Jesus Christ, so that by faith I have a new life. Help me live in grace always, not boasting in myself but depending on You every day. Lead me to live a life that pleases You and bears witness to Your glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I am saved by grace, and I will live the good life God has prepared.

t: Hope Is the Anchor of the Soul
v: In the same way, God, being determined to show more abundantly to the heirs of the promise the immutability of his counsel, interposed with an oath;
that by two unchangeable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we may have a strong encouragement, who have fled for refuge to take hold of the hope set before us.
This hope we have as an anchor of the soul, a hope both sure and steadfast and entering into that which is within the veil;
where as a forerunner Jesus entered for us, having become a high priest forever after the order of Melchizedek.
b: Life is like a ship sailing the sea: sometimes calm, sometimes storm-tossed. When the storm comes, what keeps a ship from drifting is not how beautiful it is but whether it has a firm anchor. In the same way, when life brings difficulty, disappointment, and challenge, what sustains us is not smooth circumstances but whether we have hope that comes from God.

The author tells us that God’s promises never change. People change, circumstances change, feelings change, but God does not. What he has promised, he will fulfill; what he has spoken, he will see through. Because it is impossible for God to lie, we can safely build our lives on his word.

This hope is not optimism or self-comfort; it is built on the salvation Jesus Christ has already accomplished. Jesus has entered within the veil for us, into the Father’s presence, as our high priest forever. He has opened a way to God, and he guarantees that our future is in God’s hands.

So even with storms before us, we can stand firm. Our hope is not cast into a shifting world but fastened to the unchanging Lord. When we hold on to Jesus, like a ship held by its anchor, the waves may churn, yet we will not drift away and be lost.
a: Hold on to God’s promises
Let God’s word be your daily strength and support.
Don’t let circumstances decide your mood
Turn your eyes from the storm to the Lord who rules the storm.
Reflect often on eternal hope
Remember that our future is in God’s hands.
q: When storms come in life, is my heart pulled along by circumstances, or anchored firmly by God’s promises?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for being a faithful, covenant-keeping God. When I face the storms and uncertainties of life, help me not to walk by sight but to hold on to Your promises. Thank You that Jesus has opened the way to You for me, giving me a hope that cannot be shaken. Make my heart steadfast in You, so that whatever happens, I trust You to the end. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: My hope is in Jesus, the firm and steadfast anchor of my soul.

t: Those Who Exalt Themselves Will Be Brought Low
v: The man said to Joab, “Though I should receive a thousand shekels of silver in my hand, I would not put forth my hand against the king’s son; for in our hearing the king commanded you and Abishai and Ittai, saying, ‘Beware that no one touch the young man Absalom.’
Otherwise, if I had dealt falsely against his life (and there is no matter hidden from the king), then you yourself would have set yourself against me.”
Then Joab said, “I can’t waste time like this with you.” He took three darts in his hand and thrust them through the heart of Absalom while he was yet alive in the midst of the oak.
Ten young men who bore Joab’s armor surrounded Absalom, struck him, and killed him.
Joab blew the trumpet, and the people returned from pursuing Israel, for Joab held back the people.
They took Absalom and threw him into a great pit in the forest, and laid a very great heap of stones on him. All Israel fled, everyone to his tent.

Now Absalom in his lifetime had taken and set up for himself the pillar which is in the King’s Valley, for he said, “I have no son to keep my name in memory.” He called the pillar after his own name, and it is called Absalom’s Monument to this day.
b: Absalom had everything a person could envy. He was strikingly handsome, deeply loved by the people, and the son of King David. Yet his greatest problem was not a lack of ability but the pride in his heart. He refused to submit to the authority God had established. Instead he reached for the throne, exalted himself, and finally walked the road of rebellion.

While he was still alive, Absalom set up a monument for himself, hoping his name would be remembered forever. He worked hard to build his own glory and pursue his own reputation. Yet the irony is that what people remember is not his glory but his tragic end. Those who chase their own glory often lose true glory.

Scripture reminds us again and again that pride is the beginning of a fall. Satan fell because of pride, and Absalom was destroyed by pride. Pride pulls people out of their rightful place and makes them grasp at authority that was never theirs; humility brings us back before God, acknowledging that we are only recipients of his grace.

A truly valuable life is not one in which our own name is lifted high, but one in which God’s name is glorified. When we lay down self-centeredness, stop seeking our own glory, and faithfully carry out the mission God has entrusted to us, our lives will bear eternal fruit. God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.
a: Watch for the trap of pride
Do not make self the center of your life.
Learn to submit to God
Honor the order and authority God has established.
Glorify God alone
Do not seek your own name; seek only that God be glorified.
q: Am I building my own reputation, or glorifying the name of God?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, guard my heart so that I do not fall into the trap of pride and self-centeredness. Help me see that every grace comes from You. Let me stop pursuing my own glory and lift up You alone. Give me a humble, teachable heart that is willing to submit to Your leading and faithfully fulfill the mission You have entrusted to me. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will follow the Lord with a humble heart and glorify the name of God alone.

t: The Spring of Living Water
v: A woman of Samaria came to draw water. Jesus said to her, “Give me a drink.”
(For his disciples had gone away into the city to buy food.)
The Samaritan woman therefore said to him, “How is it that you, being a Jew, ask for a drink from me, a Samaritan woman?” (For Jews have no dealings with Samaritans.)
Jesus answered her, “If you knew the gift of God, and who it is who says to you, ‘Give me a drink,’ you would have asked him, and he would have given you living water.”
Jesus answered her, “Everyone who drinks of this water will thirst again,
but whoever drinks of the water that I will give him will never thirst again; but the water that I will give him will become in him a well of water springing up to eternal life.”
The woman said to him, “Sir, give me this water, so that I don’t get thirsty, neither come all the way here to draw.”
Jesus said to her, “Go, call your husband, and come here.”
The woman answered, “I have no husband.” Jesus said to her, “You said well, ‘I have no husband,’
for you have had five husbands; and he whom you now have is not your husband. This you have said truly.”
Jesus said to her, “Woman, believe me, the hour comes, when neither in this mountain, nor in Jerusalem, will you worship the Father.
But the hour comes, and now is, when the true worshippers will worship the Father in spirit and truth, for the Father seeks such to be his worshippers.
God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and truth.”
The woman said to him, “I know that Messiah comes” (he who is called Christ). “When he has come, he will declare to us all things.”
Jesus said to her, “I am he, the one who speaks to you.”
b: The Samaritan woman came to the well to draw water, wanting only to satisfy her physical thirst, but she unexpectedly met the Savior of life. Jesus told her, “Everyone who drinks of this water will thirst again.” The things of this world can meet a passing need, but they cannot fill the emptiness deep within the human heart. Many people work hard for money, achievement, romance, and status, only to find that they are still thirsty once they have them.

The living water Jesus gives is the new life that comes from God. This water is not a supply from outside but a spring within. When a person receives Jesus, the Holy Spirit comes to live inside, bringing true peace, joy, and satisfaction. Circumstances on the outside may change, but the spring on the inside keeps flowing.

Jesus did not dodge the woman’s questions; he gently touched the wound deep in her life. He knew everything about her past, yet he did not condemn her. He led her to the truth. God’s love does not excuse sin; it heals lives in the light of truth. When we come honestly before God, we can experience his forgiveness and renewal.

Finally, Jesus told her that true worship is not about a place or a form, but about worshiping God in spirit and truth. What God seeks is not outward religious activity but a heart that truly loves and obeys him. When we let Jesus be the spring of living water in our lives, we can live in close fellowship with God.
a: Come to Jesus for satisfaction
Do not chase only outward things; seek the Lord of life.
Face your life honestly
Let God’s truth shine on your heart and heal it.
Worship God in spirit and truth
Build a real and intimate devotional life.
q: What am I using to satisfy the thirst in my heart? Have I truly come to Jesus to receive living water?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for sending Jesus to be the living water of life. When I look for satisfaction in the world and am still thirsty, draw me back to You. Help me face my life honestly and receive Your forgiveness and healing. May Your living water become a spring within me, so that I may live a full and joyful life. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Jesus is the living water of my life, and in him I will find true satisfaction.

t: Quick to Listen, Slow to Speak
v: So, my beloved brothers, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger;
for the anger of man doesn’t produce the righteousness of God.
Therefore, putting away all filthiness and overflow of wickedness, receive with humility the implanted word, which is able to save your souls.
b: James points to an important secret of spiritual growth: “Be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger.” Sadly, we often do the opposite: quick to speak, slow to listen, and easily angered. We rush to express our own opinions, unwilling to patiently hear others, and even more neglectful of the voice of God.

Listening is a form of humility. When we are willing to be still and listen to God’s word and to the needs of others, many misunderstandings and conflicts can be avoided. Many broken relationships are not caused by a lack of love, but by everyone talking and no one willing to listen.

James goes on to remind us that human anger does not produce the righteousness of God. Anger often comes from hurt, self-protection, or stubbornness, and the result is that it wounds others and costs us our own peace. True victory is not overpowering others with emotion, but letting God rule our hearts.

So we need to receive God’s word with a gentle heart. God’s word is like a seed planted in the soil of the heart. When we humbly receive it and obey it, it bears the fruit of a changed life. God’s aim is not first to change others, but to change us, making us more and more like Christ.
a: Learn to listen with your heart
Listen carefully first, then speak.
Manage your emotions
Do not let anger control your reactions.
Receive God’s word humbly
Let truth take root and grow in your life.
q: The last time something made me angry, did I react out of emotion or respond according to God’s heart?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, give me a humble, teachable heart, so that I am willing to be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to anger. Help me not to be ruled by my emotions but guided by Your truth. Plant Your word deep in my heart, so that my life becomes more like Jesus day by day. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will be quick to listen to God’s word and let Christ rule my heart.

t: Still Turning to God When We Are Hurt
v: Day and night they prowl around on its walls. Iniquity and mischief are also within it.
Wickedness is within it. Threats and lies don’t depart from its streets.
For it was not an enemy who insulted me, then I could have endured it. Neither was it he who hated me who raised himself up against me, then I would have hidden myself from him.
But it was you, a man equal to me, my companion, and my familiar friend.
We took sweet fellowship together. We walked in God’s house with the throng.
Let death come suddenly on them. Let them go down alive into Sheol, for wickedness is among them, in their dwelling.
As for me, I will call on God. Yahweh will save me.
Evening, morning, and at noon, I will complain and moan. He will hear my voice.
He has redeemed my soul in peace from the battle that was against me, although there are many who oppose me.
God, who is enthroned from ancient times, will hear and answer them. Selah. They never change, and don’t fear God.
He has put forth his hands against his friends. He has violated his covenant.
b: In this psalm David expresses deep pain. What grieved him most was not the attack of an enemy but the betrayal of a friend. It is hard enough to be hurt by an enemy, but when someone who once walked with us, worshiped with us, and trusted us suddenly turns against us, the wound often goes deeper.

Facing such pain, David did not pretend to be strong, nor did he suppress his feelings. He honestly brought his hurt, anger, and sense of injustice to God. Scripture shows us that faith does not mean having no emotions; it means choosing to come to God even in the midst of them. God can receive our tears and heal our wounds.

Most precious of all, David did not stay stuck in bitterness. He said, “As for me, I will call on God.” When people hurt him, he did not fix his eyes on them but turned to God. Human comfort is limited and human justice is limited; only God can truly execute judgment and truly give peace.

Misunderstanding, betrayal, and hurt are hard to avoid in life, but do not let a wound become a root of bitterness. Give your pain to God, give justice to God, and give your future to God. As we keep drawing near to the Lord, we will find that God’s presence is more real than people’s abandonment, and God’s comfort more powerful than people’s harm.
a: Pour out your heart to God honestly
Do not suppress your pain; bring it to God.
Do not let bitterness stay in your heart
Leave judgment and repayment to God.
Keep drawing near to God
When you are hurt, come to the Lord all the more.
q: When I am misunderstood or hurt, do I cling to the wound, or do I bring myself to God?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, when I am hurt, misunderstood, or betrayed, please heal my heart. Help me not to live in bitterness and resentment, but to give every burden to You. Thank You for understanding my tears and knowing my hurt. Fill me with Your peace, so that I can keep trusting and following You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will give my pain to God and find true peace in him.

t: Walking with the Wise
v: The teaching of the wise is a spring of life, to turn away from the snares of death.
Good understanding wins favor, but the way of the unfaithful is hard.
Every prudent man deals with knowledge, but a fool spreads out folly.
A wicked messenger falls into trouble, but a trustworthy envoy gets healing.
Poverty and shame come to him who refuses discipline, but he who heeds correction shall be honored.
Desire fulfilled is sweet to the soul, but it is detestable to fools to forsake evil.
One who walks with wise men grows wise, but the companion of fools suffers harm.
b: Proverbs tells us that wisdom is not merely knowledge but a way of life. The teaching of the wise is like a spring of life, able to keep people away from danger and traps and guide them onto the right path. Many people want to change their lives yet overlook the most important thing: letting God’s wisdom enter their lives first.

One important mark of a wise person is a willingness to be taught. The text says, “He who heeds correction shall be honored.” Our greatest limit is often not a lack of ability but an unwillingness to admit our shortcomings. The proud reject advice; the humble accept a reminder. Only a person who can hear the truth has room to grow.

Scripture also stresses the importance of companions. “One who walks with wise men grows wise, but the companion of fools suffers harm.” What kind of person we become is closely tied to the people we walk with over the long term. Whom you listen to, whom you spend time with, and whom you let influence you, you will gradually become like.

So we should seek not just successful people but people who fear God, who are wise, and who live beautiful lives, and walk with them. When we encourage, remind, and help one another grow with those who love the Lord, it is easier to stay on the path that pleases God and to live a full and blessed life.
a: Pursue God’s wisdom
Receive God’s teaching every day through Scripture and prayer.
Keep a teachable heart
Be willing to accept reminders and correction.
Choose wise companions
Walk and grow with people who fear God.
q: Do the people who influence me most lead me toward God or away from him?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, give me a wise heart, willing to listen to Your word and to accept the reminders and counsel of others. Help me stay away from foolishness and pride, and choose to walk with those who fear You. May my life grow more mature day by day and keep growing in Your truth, so that I live a life that pleases You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will walk with the wise and keep growing in God’s truth.

t: Set Your Mind on Things Above
v: If then you were raised together with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is, seated at the right hand of God.
Set your mind on the things that are above, not on the things that are on the earth.
For you died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God.
When Christ, our life, is revealed, then you will also be revealed with him in glory.
b: Paul reminds believers that since they have been raised with Christ, they should no longer live only for the things of earth as before. Many people spend every day thinking about money, work, status, gain and loss, and what others think of them, and as a result their hearts are often full of worry and pressure. It is not that these things do not matter, but they should not be the center of life.

“Setting your mind on things above” does not mean escaping reality; it means looking at life with God’s eyes. When we look only at earthly things, we are easily tossed about by circumstances; when we fix our eyes on God’s Kingdom and God’s will, we can stay steady in a changing world. Everything on earth will pass away; only what belongs to God lasts forever.

Paul goes on to say, “Christ, our life.” Christ is not just one part of our life, nor merely someone we worship on Sunday; he is the center of our life. When Jesus becomes the Lord of our life, our worth, direction, and goals are all realigned. We no longer live for ourselves; we let Christ rule within us.

Today the world keeps drawing our eyes downward, but God calls us to look up. When we set our minds on the Lord and fix our focus on eternal things, we can live with a peace and hope that rise above circumstances. True life is not found in earthly achievements; it is found in Christ.
a: Readjust your life’s focus
Seek not only earthly things but God’s Kingdom.
See things through God’s eyes
Seek God’s will in everything.
Let Christ be the center of your life
Honor the Lord above all and follow his leading.
q: Lately, what do I think about most: earthly things, or the eternal things of God’s Kingdom?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for raising me with Christ and giving me new life. Help me not to let the things of the world fill my mind, but to set my mind on things above. In my daily life, let Jesus be my center and eternity my direction, so that I live a life that pleases You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will set my mind on things above and let Christ be the center of my life.

t: Eyes Fixed on God Alone
v: Our God, will you not judge them? For we have no might against this great company that comes against us; neither do we know what to do, but our eyes are on you.”
All Judah stood before Yahweh, with their little ones, their wives, and their children.
Then the Spirit of Yahweh came on Jahaziel the son of Zechariah, the son of Benaiah, the son of Jeiel, the son of Mattaniah, the Levite of the sons of Asaph, in the midst of the assembly.

He said, “Listen, all Judah, and you inhabitants of Jerusalem, and you, King Jehoshaphat! Yahweh says to you, ‘Don’t be afraid, and don’t be dismayed because of this great multitude; for the battle is not yours, but God’s.
Tomorrow, go down against them. Behold, they come up by the ascent of Ziz. You will find them at the end of the valley, before the wilderness of Jeruel.

You will not need to fight in this battle. Set yourselves, stand still, and see the salvation of Yahweh with you, O Judah and Jerusalem. Don’t be afraid, nor be dismayed. Go out against them tomorrow, for Yahweh is with you.’”
Jehoshaphat bowed his head with his face to the ground. All Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem fell down before Yahweh, worshipping Yahweh.
The Levites, of the children of the Kohathites and of the children of the Korahites, stood up to praise Yahweh, the God of Israel, with an exceedingly loud voice.
b: When a mighty enemy army drew near, Jehoshaphat did not rely on his own strength, nor did he rush to look for human solutions. He admitted to God, “We have no might against this great company… neither do we know what to do.” This is not a sign of weakness but the beginning of true faith, because only when people admit their limits do they truly lean on God’s power.

Then Jehoshaphat said something very precious: “Our eyes are on you.” Many times our eyes stay fixed on the problem, so the more we look the more afraid we become; they stay fixed on circumstances, so the more we look the more discouraged we become. But faith does not deny that difficulties exist; it keeps looking to God in the face of them.

Through the prophet God declared, “Don’t be afraid, and don’t be dismayed because of this great multitude; for the battle is not yours, but God’s.” What mattered in this battle was not how large Judah’s army was but whether God was with them. Life is often like this: some problems are beyond our ability, and some challenges cannot be solved by human wisdom, yet God still holds everything in his hands.

What is moving is that before the victory had come, the people had already bowed down in worship and praised God with a loud voice. They did not worship after seeing the result; they worshiped because they believed God’s promise. True faith keeps believing that God will accomplish his purpose even before the answer appears.
a: Admit your limits
Do not tough it out; bring your burden to God.
Fix your eyes on God
Do not keep staring at the difficulty; look to the Lord who rules over it.
Respond to faith with praise
While waiting for God to work, keep worshiping him.
q: In the difficulty I face now, are my eyes on the problem or on God?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, when I face difficulties beyond my ability, help me not to rely on myself or give in to fear. Teach me, like Jehoshaphat, to admit my limits and look to You alone. Thank You for promising to be with me and to fight for me. Give me faith and courage, so that even while I wait I will keep worshiping and trusting You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: My eyes are on God alone, for victory belongs to the Lord.

t: By Faith, Moving Toward the Promise
v: By faith, Abraham, when he was called, obeyed to go out to a place which he was to receive for an inheritance. He went out, not knowing where he went.
By faith, he lived as an alien in the land of promise, as in a land not his own, living in tents with Isaac and Jacob, the heirs with him of the same promise.
For he looked for the city which has the foundations, whose builder and maker is God.
By faith, even Sarah herself received power to conceive, and she bore a child when she was past age, since she counted him faithful who had promised.
Therefore as many were born from one man, and him as good as dead, as many as the stars of the sky in multitude, and as the sand which is by the sea shore innumerable.
These all died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them and embraced them from afar, and having confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.
For those who say such things make it clear that they are seeking a country of their own.
If indeed they had been thinking of that country from which they went out, they would have had enough time to return.
But now they desire a better country, that is, a heavenly one. Therefore God is not ashamed of them, to be called their God, for he has prepared a city for them.
b: Abraham’s greatest mark was not ability but faith. When God called him to leave his familiar homeland, he did not even know where he was going, yet he chose to obey. Faith does not move forward only after seeing; it moves forward because it trusts God. When the future cannot be seen, faith holds on to God’s promise.

Sarah was the same. From a human point of view, she was long past childbearing age and could not possibly have another child. Yet she believed God’s promise and so experienced a miracle. Faith is not believing in how capable we are; it is believing that the One who promised is faithful. The end of human ability is often the beginning of God’s work.

These heroes of faith shared one thing: all their lives they moved toward God’s promise. Although some promises were not fully fulfilled in their lifetimes, they saw them from afar and welcomed them with joy. They knew they were only strangers on earth, and that their true home was not in this world but in the eternal Kingdom God had prepared.

Today we also live on the same journey of faith. Some prayers have not yet been answered, some hopes have not yet been fulfilled, and some promises still seem far away. But do not lose heart, for God has never failed to keep his word. As we keep looking to him and following him, we will find that the greatest blessing in life is not only receiving the promise, but coming to know more deeply the faithful God along the way.
a: Obey God’s leading
Take a step of faith even when you cannot see ahead.
Hold on to God’s promises
Believe that what God has said will come to pass.
Make eternity your life’s direction
Do not live only for earthly things; seek God’s Kingdom.
q: Am I walking by faith right now, or only willing to take the path I can see?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that You are a faithful, covenant-keeping God. When I cannot see the road ahead, give me faith like Abraham’s, willing to obey Your leading, and faith like Sarah’s, believing that Your promises will never fail. Help me look beyond the present and fix my eyes on the eternal home You have prepared. May I follow You all my life, until I see You face to face. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will follow God by faith, believing that his promises will surely be fulfilled.

t: Walking the Path of Integrity
v: Blessings are on the head of the righteous, but violence covers the mouth of the wicked.
The memory of the righteous is blessed, but the name of the wicked will rot.
The wise in heart will accept commandments, but a chattering fool will fall.
He who walks blamelessly walks surely, but he who perverts his ways will be found out.
One who winks with the eye causes sorrow, but a chattering fool will fall.
The mouth of the righteous is a spring of life, but violence covers the mouth of the wicked.
Hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all wrongdoing.
Wisdom is found on the lips of him who has understanding, but a rod is for the back of him who is void of understanding.
Wise men lay up knowledge, but the mouth of the foolish is near ruin.
b: Proverbs keeps setting two roads before us: the road of the righteous and the road of the wicked, the road of the wise and the road of the foolish. The two roads may not look very different at first, but where they end is completely different. The road of the righteous grows steadier, while the road of the wicked is finally exposed.

The text says in particular, “He who walks blamelessly walks surely.” True peace does not come from smooth circumstances but from an untroubled heart. When a person lives in the light, honest before God and others, there is nothing to hide, nothing to fake, and no fear of a secret being revealed. A person of integrity sleeps soundly because his conscience is at peace.

Proverbs also reminds us how much our words matter. The mouth of the righteous is a spring of life, bringing encouragement, comfort, and blessing; the mouth of a fool brings hurt, strife, and ruin. One word that builds up can warm a wounded heart; one word that tears down can leave a lasting scar. That is why the wise know how to manage their words.

Finally, Solomon tells us, “Hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all wrongdoing.” Hatred makes people keep magnifying others’ faults, but love is willing to forgive and bear with them. When we live in God’s love, we no longer meet others with criticism and judgment, but build relationships with grace and compassion. Such a life can truly become a blessing to others.
a: Choose the path of integrity
Be honest and upright in everything, living in God’s light.
Manage your words
Speak more words that build up and fewer that hurt.
Replace hatred with love
Learn to forgive and bear with others, and build peaceful relationships.
q: Do my words and actions bring a spring of life, or strife and hurt?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, give me a wise heart, so that I choose to walk the path of integrity. Guard my mouth, so that I speak words that build up and not words that hurt. Fill me with Your love, so that I learn to forgive, bear with, and accept others. May my life be a vessel that blesses others and brings glory to Your name. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will walk the path of integrity and let my life be a blessing to others.

t: Wait for the Lord and Renew Your Strength
v: (By David.) Yahweh is my light and my salvation. Whom shall I fear? Yahweh is the strength of my life. Of whom shall I be afraid?
When evildoers came at me to eat up my flesh, my adversaries and my foes, they stumbled and fell.
Though an army should encamp against me, my heart shall not fear. Though war should rise against me, even then I will be confident.
I am still confident of this: I will see the goodness of Yahweh in the land of the living.
Wait for Yahweh. Be strong, and let your heart take courage. Yes, wait for Yahweh.
b: David’s life went through countless dangers. He was hunted by Saul, and he faced attacks from foreign enemies and rebellion from within. Yet in the midst of these storms he made a firm declaration: “Yahweh is my light and my salvation. Whom shall I fear?” David’s peace did not come from safe circumstances but from God being with him.

Light drives away darkness, salvation rescues from danger, and a stronghold brings security. When David fixed his eyes on God, his enemies and the crises were still there, but fear no longer ruled his heart. True faith does not deny problems; it keeps believing that God is greater than the problem.

David also admitted that he had times of weakness. He said, “I am still confident of this: I will see the goodness of Yahweh in the land of the living.” What kept him going was not his own willpower but hope in God’s grace. He believed that God still reigns, still shows kindness, and is still at work.

So David finally gave a reminder to himself and to all God’s children: “Wait for Yahweh.” Waiting is not passive; it means looking to God, depending on God, and obeying God with faith. In the waiting, God strengthens our hearts so that we do not lose heart because of circumstances, but grow ever stronger in hope.
a: Keep your focus on God
Do not keep staring at the difficulty; fix your eyes on the Lord.
Believe God’s goodness is still there
Even if you have not yet seen the answer, believe God is at work.
Learn to wait for God
In prayer and trust, let God strengthen your heart.
q: In the challenges I face now, am I afraid of my circumstances, or trusting in God’s presence?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that You are my light, my salvation, and my stronghold. When I face difficulties and the unknown, help me not to be controlled by fear but to look to You in faith. Strengthen my heart, so that I do not lose heart while waiting and do not lose courage while hoping. May I experience Your goodness and presence every day. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will wait for the Lord, believing I will see his goodness in the land of the living.

t: The Lord Who Never Changes
v: Of the angels he says, “Who makes his angels winds, and his servants a flame of fire.”
But of the Son he says, “Your throne, God, is forever and ever. The scepter of uprightness is the scepter of your kingdom.
You have loved righteousness, and hated iniquity. Therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your fellows.”
And, “You, Lord, in the beginning, laid the foundation of the earth. The heavens are the works of your hands.
They will perish, but you continue. They all will grow old like a garment does.
As a mantle, you will roll them up, and they will be changed; but you are the same. Your years will not fail.”
But which of the angels has he told at any time, “Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies the footstool of your feet?”
Aren’t they all serving spirits, sent out to do service for the sake of those who will inherit salvation?
b: Hebrews begins by exalting the honor and greatness of Jesus Christ. The author tells us that angels, though glorious, are only God’s servants; Jesus alone is the eternal King. His throne lasts forever and ever, his Kingdom is full of righteousness, and he is worthy of all worship and glory.

This passage stresses one precious truth: “You are the same.” Heaven and earth change, times change, circumstances change, and human hearts change. What we have today we may lose tomorrow; what is stable today may shake tomorrow. But Jesus Christ never changes, and his love, faithfulness, and promises last forever.

Because the Lord does not change, our faith has a foundation. If God were as fickle as people, we could never truly trust him. But through mountaintops and valleys, in good times and bad, God is always the Lord who keeps covenant and shows steadfast love. As he led us yesterday, he leads us today, and he will lead us to the end.

The passage ends by saying that angels are sent to serve those who will inherit salvation. This shows us that God is not only seated high on his throne, but also tenderly cares for his children. He rules the whole universe, and he also cares about our needs each day. When we know this unchanging Lord, we can live with security and hope in a changing world.
a: Build your faith on Christ
Do not depend on people and things that change.
Believe God never changes
His promises are still valid today.
Rest in God’s care
Believe the Lord is guiding and keeping you.
q: When circumstances change, is my heart still firmly built on Christ?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for revealing Your glory and faithfulness through Jesus Christ. When the world keeps changing and people come and go, thank You that You never change. Help me build my faith on You, not shaken by circumstances or discouraged by difficulties. May I trust You every day and experience Your everlasting love and care. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will trust the Lord who never changes, for his faithfulness lasts forever.

t: Jesus Is the Way, the Truth, and the Life
v: Thomas said to him, “Lord, we don’t know where you are going. How can we know the way?”
Jesus said to him, “I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father, but by me.
If you had known me, you would have known my Father also. From now on, you know him, and have seen him.”
Philip said to him, “Lord, show us the Father, and that will be enough for us.”
Jesus said to him, “Have I been with you so long, and do you not know me, Philip? He who has seen me has seen the Father. How do you say, ‘Show us the Father?’
Don’t you believe that I am in the Father, and the Father in me? The words that I tell you I speak not from myself; but the Father who lives in me does his works.
Believe me that I am in the Father, and the Father in me; or else believe me for the very works’ sake.”
b: The disciples’ hearts were full of confusion. They wanted to know where to go, and how to find God. This is really the question of many people: Where is the direction for my life? Where is truth? And where is the meaning of life? Jesus did not give them a theory, nor did he point to a road on a map. He said directly, “I am the way, the truth, and the life.”

Jesus is the way because he brings us to the Father. The greatest human problem is not failing to find a road to success, but being separated from God. Through the cross Jesus opened a way back into the Father’s arms, so that we can be reconciled to God again.

Jesus is the truth because he does not merely teach truth; he is truth in person. In a world full of confusion and competing voices, people easily lose their way. But when we know Jesus, we can know God’s heart and see life, the world, and ourselves through God’s eyes.

Jesus is the life because he gives new, eternal life. Everything in the world will pass away, but life in Christ never fades. When Jesus becomes the Lord of our life, we receive not only eternal life in the future, but from today a full life with direction and hope.
a: Follow Jesus, the Way
In every decision of life, seek the Lord’s leading.
Take Jesus as your standard of truth
Let God’s word be the basis for judging right and wrong.
Receive life from Jesus
Walk with the Lord each day and draw on heavenly strength.
q: When I face life’s choices, do I rely on my own judgment, or follow Jesus, the Way?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for revealing Yourself to us through Jesus. Thank You that Jesus is the way, so that I can come to You; the truth, so that I am no longer lost; and the life, so that I have an eternal hope. Help me know You, follow You, and depend on You every day, and let Jesus truly be the center of my life. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Jesus is my way, my truth, and my life, and I will follow him all my days.

t: Responding Courageously to God’s Call
v: Now Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lappidoth, judged Israel at that time.
She lived under Deborah’s palm tree between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim. The children of Israel came up to her for judgment.

She sent and called Barak the son of Abinoam out of Kedesh Naphtali, and said to him, “Hasn’t Yahweh, the God of Israel, commanded, ‘Go and lead the way to Mount Tabor, and take with you ten thousand men of the children of Naphtali and of the children of Zebulun?
I will draw to you, to the river Kishon, Sisera, the captain of Jabin’s army, with his chariots and his multitude; and I will deliver him into your hand.’”
Barak said to her, “If you will go with me, then I will go; but if you will not go with me, I will not go.”

She said, “I will surely go with you; nevertheless the journey that you take won’t be for your honor; for Yahweh will sell Sisera into the hand of a woman.” Deborah arose, and went with Barak to Kedesh.

Deborah said to Barak, “Go! For this is the day in which Yahweh has delivered Sisera into your hand. Hasn’t Yahweh gone out before you?” So Barak went down from Mount Tabor, and ten thousand men after him.
b: At that time Israel was oppressed by Jabin, the Canaanite king, and his commander Sisera, and the people lived in fear. God raised up Deborah as judge and prophet to lead the people back to him. She had not only spiritual insight but also courageous faith, believing that God’s promise would surely come to pass.

God had clearly called Barak to lead an army into battle and promised victory, yet Barak was still afraid. He said to Deborah, “If you will go with me, then I will go.” This shows that he depended more on a person he could see than on God alone. Yet God did not give up on him, and through Deborah kept encouraging him to move forward.

The key sentence comes in verse 14: “Hasn’t Yahweh gone out before you?” What brought Barak victory was not ten thousand soldiers, nor Deborah’s company, but that God had already gone ahead. Faith is not believing that we ourselves are capable; it is believing that God has already gone ahead to open the way.

Today God often calls us to take a step of faith as well. Many times, like Barak, we shrink back when we see difficulty and are afraid when we see a challenge. But God reminds us not to look only at our own ability but at his presence. When God leads from the front, we can go forward courageously and experience his victory.
a: Respond to God’s call
Do not miss God’s leading because of fear.
Build your faith on God
Do not over-depend on people; depend on God.
Courageously take the first step
Believe that God has already gone ahead of you.
q: Has God recently stirred me to do something that I keep putting off out of fear?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that You are the God who goes before me. When I face challenges and the unknown, take away my timidity and unbelief, and give me a courageous heart. Help me look not only at my own limits but at Your presence and promises. May I, like Deborah, believe Your word, and like Barak, finally be willing to obey Your leading. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will courageously respond to God’s call, for the Lord has already gone before me.

t: Casting Your Anxiety on God
v: Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time;
casting all your worries on him, because he cares for you.
Be sober and self-controlled. Be watchful. Your adversary, the devil, walks around like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour.
Withstand him steadfast in your faith, knowing that your brothers who are in the world are undergoing the same sufferings.
But may the God of all grace, who called you to his eternal glory by Christ Jesus, after you have suffered a little while, make you perfect, confirm, strengthen, and establish you.
To him be the glory and the power forever and ever. Amen.
b: Peter urges believers that when facing difficulty and pressure, the first thing is not to tough it out on our own but to learn to humble ourselves under God’s mighty hand. Behind much anxiety is really the desire to control everything ourselves. But God wants us to admit our limits and believe that he is still in control. At the time he has set, he will accomplish his purpose himself.

So Peter says, “Casting all your worries on him, because he cares for you.” What a precious promise! Not just some of our worries, but all of them; and not that God reluctantly puts up with them, but that he truly cares for us. Every burden, every tear, every struggle, he knows.

Peter also reminds us that spiritual warfare is real. The devil wants people to live in fear, discouragement, and unbelief, so we must stay alert and resist him with steadfast faith. The enemy’s greatest trick is often not to destroy us directly, but to make us forget God’s faithfulness and keep our eyes on the problem.

But Peter finally brings the focus back to God’s grace. Present suffering is only temporary, while God’s glory is eternal. The God of all grace will not leave us; he will himself make us complete, confirm us, strengthen us, and establish us. Today’s tears are not the end of the story; God’s grace is.
a: Give your worries to God
Do not carry your burdens alone.
Stay alert
Do not let fear and discouragement take over your life.
Keep trusting God
Believe God will accomplish his good purpose at the right time.
q: Are there still worries I am clinging to and have not truly handed over to God?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for caring about every part of my life. Help me learn to humbly depend on You and no longer carry my burdens alone. When I face anxiety, temptation, and difficulty, strengthen my faith so that I fix my eyes on You. Thank You for promising that after a little suffering You will Yourself make me complete, confirm me, and give me strength. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will cast all my worries on God, because he cares for me.

t: Carefully Keeping and Doing God’s Word
v: Now, Israel, listen to the statutes and to the ordinances which I teach you, to do them, that you may live and go in and possess the land which Yahweh, the God of your fathers, gives you.
You shall not add to the word which I command you, neither shall you take away from it, that you may keep the commandments of Yahweh your God which I command you.

Keep therefore and do them; for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the peoples, who shall hear all these statutes, and say, ‘Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.’
For what great nation is there that has a god so near to them as Yahweh our God is whenever we call on him?
What great nation is there, that has statutes and ordinances so righteous as all this law which I set before you this day?

Only take heed to yourself, and keep your soul diligently, lest you forget the things which your eyes saw, and lest they depart from your heart all the days of your life; but make them known to your children and your children’s children:

the day that you stood before Yahweh your God in Horeb, when Yahweh said to me, ‘Assemble the people to me, and I will make them hear my words, that they may learn to fear me all the days that they live on the earth, and that they may teach their children.’
b: Just before Israel entered the Promised Land, Moses reminded them once more of the most important thing: not military power, not wealth and resources, but listening to and obeying God’s word. God’s word is not human opinion; it is the way of life. When people obey God’s word, they walk toward life; when they turn from it, they easily lose their way.

God specifically told the people not to add to his word or take away from it. People often like to obey selectively, accepting the parts they like and ignoring the parts they don’t. But true faith does not revise God’s truth to suit ourselves; it adjusts ourselves to obey God’s truth.

Moses went on to say that keeping God’s word is the greatest wisdom. The world builds wisdom on knowledge, education, and experience, but Scripture tells us that true wisdom is fearing God and living according to his heart. When God’s people live out the life of truth, they become a witness to the world and let people see the glory of God.

Finally, Moses reminded them not to forget what God had done, and to pass their faith on to the next generation. Faith is not only a personal blessing; it is a mission passed from one generation to the next. When we live out God’s word ourselves and also teach our children to know God, a life that fears God can be handed down again and again.
a: Read God’s word earnestly
Spend time each day receiving God’s teaching.
Obey God’s word
Do not only understand the truth; put it into practice.
Pass on the faith
Share God’s grace and truth with the next generation.
q: Am I listening to God’s word, or doing God’s word? Is my life a witness to the truth?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for giving us Your precious word. Help me be not only a hearer but a doer of the word. Let me revere Your word and obey it, and live out Your truth in daily life. Help me also pass on the faith to the next generation, so that more people see Your glory through my life. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will carefully keep and do God’s word and live a wise life in his truth.

t: Placing Myself in God’s Hands
v: (For the Chief Musician. A Psalm by David.) In you, Yahweh, I take refuge. Let me never be disappointed. Deliver me in your righteousness.
Bow down your ear to me. Deliver me speedily. Be to me a strong rock, a stronghold to save me.
For you are my rock and my fortress; therefore for your name’s sake lead me and guide me.
Pluck me out of the net that they have laid secretly for me, for you are my stronghold.
Into your hand I commit my spirit. You redeem me, Yahweh, God of truth.
I will be glad and rejoice in your lovingkindness, for you have seen my affliction. You have known my soul in adversities.
You haven’t shut me up into the hand of the enemy. You have set my feet in a broad place.
Have mercy on me, Yahweh, for I am in distress. My eye is consumed with grief, yes, my soul and my body.
For my life is spent with sorrow, and my years with sighing. My strength fails because of my iniquity, and my bones are consumed.
Because of all my adversaries I have become a reproach, yes, to my neighbors exceedingly, and a fear to my friends. Those who saw me on the street fled from me.
I am forgotten from their hearts like a dead man. I am like broken pottery.
For I have heard the whisper of many, terror on every side, while they conspire together against me, they plot to take away my life.
b: When David wrote this psalm, he was going through great pain and pressure. He was misunderstood, attacked, and forgotten, and felt worn out in body and spirit. Yet in such circumstances he did not give up his faith; he chose to come to God and say, “Into your hand I commit my spirit.”

There are many times in life when we cannot control our circumstances or change what others think. When misunderstanding comes, pressure grows heavy, and the road ahead is unclear, it is easy to fall into worry and fear. But David reminds us that true peace does not come from a change in circumstances; it comes from entrusting ourselves to the faithful God.

David knew that God saw his affliction and knew the distress in his soul. Sometimes others do not understand us, but God does; others forget us, but God remembers; others leave us, but God is still with us. God sees not only the problems on the outside but also the tears and struggles deep within.

So even in the darkest hour, David still called God his rock, fortress, and stronghold. When we place the sovereignty of our lives in God’s hands, we can find rest even in the storm. For God’s hand is greater than our circumstances, God’s grace is deeper than our troubles, and God’s faithfulness never changes.
a: Give your burdens to God
Do not bear life’s pressure alone.
Believe God sees your struggles
He understands your tears and your struggles.
Let God be your stronghold
Keep trusting him even in hardship.
q: Lately, what am I still clinging to and have not truly placed in God’s hands?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that You are my rock, my fortress, and my stronghold. When I feel weary, wronged, or alone, help me place myself completely in Your hands. Thank You for seeing my distress and understanding my struggles. May Your peace fill me, so that in every circumstance I can trust You and follow You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will place my life in God’s hands, for he is my stronghold forever.

t: New Every Morning
v: Remember my affliction and my misery, the wormwood and the bitterness.
My soul still remembers them, and is bowed down within me.
This I recall to my mind; therefore I have hope.
It is of Yahweh’s lovingkindnesses that we are not consumed, because his compassions don’t fail.
They are new every morning; great is your faithfulness.
“Yahweh is my portion,” says my soul. “Therefore I will hope in him.”
Yahweh is good to those who wait for him, to the soul who seeks him.
It is good that a man should hope and quietly wait for the salvation of Yahweh.
b: When Jeremiah wrote these words, he was not in good times; he was in the dark hour when Jerusalem had been destroyed and his nation had suffered disaster. Recalling his affliction and sorrow, his heart was heavy and full of pain. Yet in the very midst of despair he made an important choice: he turned his eyes from suffering to God.

He said, “This I recall to my mind; therefore I have hope.” Circumstances did not change at once, but when he remembered God’s love, compassion, and faithfulness, hope returned to his heart. True hope does not come from improving circumstances; it comes from God’s unchanging character. However long the night, God’s love is still there; however hard the road, God’s compassion never ends.

The most precious line is: “They are new every morning.” Yesterday’s failures, yesterday’s tears, and yesterday’s burdens are not the end of life. Every morning God prepares new grace, new strength, and new opportunities for his children. God’s grace never runs out, and his faithfulness is always enough for us.

So Jeremiah chose to wait on God and hope in him. Waiting does not mean doing nothing; it means continuing to believe that God is at work when we cannot see the answer. When we learn to seek the Lord quietly, we will find that God’s grace often comes at the most unexpected times.
a: Turn your eyes from difficulty to God
Do not keep dwelling on pain; think on God’s faithfulness.
Believe God has new grace every day
Do not be bound by yesterday’s failures.
Learn to wait quietly on the Lord
Look to God’s salvation in prayer.
q: Today, do I think most about my difficulties, or about God’s love and faithfulness?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for being with me even in my weakest moments. When I am discouraged by circumstances, help me remember Your love and faithfulness. Thank You for giving new grace every day, so that I am not consumed. Teach me to wait on You and look to You, and in Your presence to find hope and strength again. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: God’s grace is new every day; I will look to him and go forward full of hope.

t: Glorify God in Your Body
v: “All things are lawful for me,” but not all things are expedient. “All things are lawful for me,” but I will not be brought under the power of anything.
“Foods for the belly, and the belly for foods,” but God will bring to nothing both it and them. But the body is not for sexual immorality, but for the Lord; and the Lord for the body.
Now God raised up the Lord, and will also raise us up by his power.
Don’t you know that your bodies are members of Christ? Shall I then take the members of Christ, and make them members of a prostitute? May it never be!
Or don’t you know that he who is joined to a prostitute is one body? For, “The two”, says he, “will become one flesh.”
But he who is joined to the Lord is one spirit.
Flee sexual immorality! “Every sin that a man does is outside the body,” but he who commits sexual immorality sins against his own body.
Or don’t you know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit which is in you, which you have from God? You are not your own,
for you were bought with a price. Therefore glorify God in your body and in your spirit, which are God’s.
b: Paul reminds believers that freedom does not mean doing whatever we please. Many people think, “If I like it, what’s wrong with it?” But those who belong to God ask, “Is this good for my life? Is this thing mastering me?” True freedom is not following our desires but not being enslaved by them.

Paul points out in particular that our bodies do not belong to ourselves but to the Lord. When Jesus shed his blood and gave his life on the cross, we were bought at a great price. So we no longer live as we please but let the Lord rule in our lives. The body is not a tool for satisfying desires but a vessel for serving and glorifying God.

The passage goes further: “Your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit.” In the Old Testament, God’s glory filled the temple; today, the Holy Spirit lives in every believer. What a noble identity! So how we use our bodies, and how we manage our thoughts and our lifestyle, should all reflect God’s holiness and glory.

When we are joined to the Lord, we no longer let sin rule our lives. A truly blessed life is not one of self-indulgence but one in which Jesus is King. When we offer our bodies to the Lord and live a holy life, we can be a witness to God’s glory.
a: Do not be mastered by anything
Stay away from habits and temptations that bind your life.
Value who you are
Remember you are a child of God, bought at a great price.
Glorify God with your body
Live a holy life in thought, word, and deed.
q: Is there anything in my life that is mastering me and keeping me from fully obeying God?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for buying me with the precious blood of Jesus Christ. Help me remember that my body is the temple of the Holy Spirit, and no longer live by selfish desires but live for You. Give me strength to overcome temptation, and guard my thoughts and conduct, so that every day I can glorify Your name. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I was bought with a price, and I will glorify God in my body.

t: Go and Make Disciples of All Nations
v: But the eleven disciples went into Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had sent them.
When they saw him, they bowed down to him, but some doubted.
Jesus came to them and spoke to them, saying, “All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth.
Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
teaching them to observe all things that I commanded you. Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” Amen.
b: This passage is called the Great Commission, the most important charge Jesus left the church after his resurrection. It is worth noting that when the disciples saw the risen Lord, “some doubted.” This shows us that God calls people to serve him not because they are already perfect, but he uses people in their weakness and imperfection.

Jesus first declared, “All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth.” The foundation of the Great Commission is not human ability but Christ’s authority. On our own, we have no power to change anyone’s life; but when we obey the Lord’s sending, we have power and grace from God.

Jesus told the disciples to go and make disciples of all nations. He wants not only people who decide to believe, but people who learn to follow the Lord, imitate him, and obey his words. The gospel is not only for saving people but for changing lives. A true disciple is not someone who merely knows about Jesus but someone who lives out the life of Jesus.

Finally, Jesus gave us a most precious promise: “Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” When we answer the Lord’s call, whether at home, at work, in the church, or in daily life, we do not go forward alone. The Lord himself is with us, our strength and help.
a: Respond to the Lord’s Great Commission
Be willing to share the gospel and God’s love with those around you.
Live out the life of a disciple
Not only believe in Jesus but imitate him.
Depend on the Lord’s presence
Rely on the Lord’s power in serving and witnessing.
q: Am I helping the people around me know Jesus better and follow him more closely?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for entrusting the precious gospel to us through Jesus. Help me not only receive grace but become one who shares it. Give me a heart that loves souls and sees the needs of those around me. Help me first become a true follower of the Lord and live out the life of Christ. Thank You for promising to be with us always, to the end of the age. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will follow Jesus, and I will lead more people to follow Jesus.

t: Rise Up and Bear Witness for the Lord
v: One Ananias, a devout man according to the law, well reported of by all the Jews who lived there,
came to me, and standing by me said to me, ‘Brother Saul, receive your sight!’ In that very hour I looked up at him.
He said, ‘The God of our fathers has appointed you to know his will, and to see the Righteous One, and to hear a voice from his mouth.
For you will be a witness for him to all men of what you have seen and heard.
Now why do you wait? Arise, be baptized, and wash away your sins, calling on the name of the Lord.’
b: Paul was once a persecutor of Christians, but on the road to Damascus he met the risen Lord Jesus and his life was completely changed. When Ananias came to him, he not only healed his eyes but also declared God’s call: God had chosen him to know God’s will and to be a witness for the Lord.

When God saves a person, it is not only to change his fate but to use his life. After Paul received grace, God did not want him to stay in thankfulness and enjoying grace; he sent him out to share what he had seen and heard. In fact every believer has the same mission: to bear witness to what God has done in his or her life.

Ananias then said, “Why do you wait?” Many people know God’s prompting yet keep waiting for a better time; they know they should obey but always think, “later.” Yet God often calls us to respond at once. The biggest obstacle to obedience is not ignorance of God’s will but unwillingness to take the step of faith.

Paul later became one of the most influential apostles in history, not because he was exceptionally able but because he was willing to answer God’s call. God calls us in the same way today, to be witnesses for Jesus at home, at work, in the church, and in daily life. When we are willing to obey, God can bless many more people through us.
a: Understand God’s call
Believe God has a good plan for your life.
Share your testimony
Courageously tell what God has done in your life.
Delay obedience no longer
Respond today to God’s prompting and leading.
q: What has God been prompting me to do lately? Am I still hesitating and delaying?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for choosing me, saving me, and giving me new life. Help me understand Your will and no longer live only for myself. Give me courage to share Your grace and be a witness for Jesus Christ. If I have been hesitating and delaying, help me by faith to obey Your leading. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will courageously answer God’s call and be a witness for Jesus Christ.
